system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

Need for, and Objectives of, the Final Rules 2. In this Third Report and Order, the Commission adopts rules to empower alert originators to enhance the utility of Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) as an alerting tool, making WEA more accessible and enabling WEA to provide more personalized alerts. Specifically, we require Participating Commercial Mobile Service Providers (Participating CMS Providers) to enable alerting authorities to display translated Alert Message content via the use of emergency alert message templates. In addition, our efforts to make WEA messages more accessibility extend to the deaf and hard of hearing community pursuant to our requirement that Participating CMS Providers’ WEA-capable mobile devices support templates in American Sign Language (ASL). We conclude that enabling the display of translated Alert Message content via the use of emergency alert message templates will allow alert originators to inform those communities that primarily speak a language other than English or Spanish of emergencies and save more lives. The Commission also adopts rules to require Participating CMS Providers’ WEA-capable mobile devices to support the presentation of WEA messages that link the recipient to a native mapping application. This requirement will allow alert originators to personalize alerts, spurring people to take protective action more quickly and to understand whether an alert applies to their them.

[CAPCP#0080] Canadian Profile of the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP-CP): Introduction and Rule Set 1.0 (Draft 2) (Rule #5. <info> blocks must specify the content language):
Multilingual messages must use separate <info> blocks for each language, with all non free-form text elements repeated verbatim in each block. Mixing public display content or text from different languages within the same <info> block is not allowed, except for inherently multilingual content (people, places, things) that may or may not include accented characters.

data.summary: The Arabic headline, description and instruction match the English in meaning. The visibility figure (below 2,000 m), the area (some coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi), the end time (until 19:00 today, 4 March), the wind (fresh to strong northwesterly), the hazard (blowing dust and sand) and the protective action (take extra care when driving on open roads; visibility may drop suddenly) all agree, and the URL is unchanged. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named person who reads Arabic must still review and approve it before it is sent; this review does not replace that sign-off.

no_basis.concern: The source is left as the Latin acronym 'NCM' in the Arabic description ('المصدر: NCM'). Some Arabic-only readers may not recognise it. The human reviewer may want the Arabic name (المركز الوطني للأرصاد) added. The meaning does not differ from the English.
no_basis.searched_for: Clauses requiring source or agency names to be localised in translated alert text; none of the clauses shown addresses this.
